headline: Benchmarks expose subject heterogeneity and robustness limits in EEG and neural decoders
label: Neural Decoder Benchmarks For Bci
summary: Frozen-encoder personalization, sleep-staging constraints and multi-recording decoder benchmarks are standardizing EEG and neural decoding evaluation.
synthesis: Across these preprints, the dominant thread is evaluation of EEG and neural decoders beyond held-out accuracy. A large standardized motor-imagery benchmark across three public datasets reports subject-level heterogeneity and applies portfolio-based reduction of the search space. BEND-BCI benchmarks 23 neural decoders across 16 recordings, scoring robustness, cost and cross-recording latent consistency. COFETT, a 128-channel EEG benchmark, is introduced to better separate model performance, and EEG-to-text decoding without teacher forcing is shown to be feasible. StageGuard adds physiologically constrained soft transition penalties and a semi-Markov decoder to any sleep-staging backbone. A trunk-agnostic Bayesian personalization API for frozen EEG encoders is tested on five classical trunks and REVE. What is new is the shift toward multi-dimensional, cross-dataset evaluation and modular wrappers over existing backbones.
